public_rationale: TruthfulQA's 2021 study found false answers in several model families, including GPT-2 and GPT-3 [e1]. OpenAI's March 2023 report acknowledged GPT-4's factual and reasoning errors [e2]. Reporting documents one SearchGPT demonstration error on July 25, 2024 [e5]. A study available in March 2024 found limits in reasoning self-correction without external feedback [e3]. A May 2024 study reported improved arithmetic reasoning through structured verification, qualifying the claim that models cannot check answers [e4]. Reporting on the May 19, 2025 ruling describes ChatGPT's false accusation against Walters and explains why his defamation claim failed [e6]. These records do not establish recurring failures in every listed category throughout the population released by July 28, 2024 [e1, e2, e5, e6]. The verification studies neither establish the claimed causal contribution across that population nor provide a decisive counterexample, leaving the claim unresolved [e3, e4].
limitations: The packet lacks exhaustive model coverage and evidence of every listed failure category, especially false personal accusations [e1, e2, e5, e6].
The verification studies concern selected models, tasks and procedures; they do not isolate a cause across the full historical population [e3, e4].
The SearchGPT report documents one demonstration, which cannot establish recurrence [e5].
The Walters evidence is later reporting on a court ruling. False accusations and legally actionable defamation are distinct [e6].

statement.excerpt: The lack of sanity-checking leads them to flub arithmetic, to make boneheaded errors, to make stuff up, to occasionally defame people, and so on — over and over again, in literally every transformer that has been released, from GPT-2 to GPT-3 to GPT-4 to the latest system SearchGPT.
statement.document_title: AlphaProof, AlphaGeometry, ChatGPT, and why the future of AI is neurosymbolic

from_speaker: The lack of sanity-checking leads them
in literally every transformer that has been released
from GPT-2 to GPT-3 to GPT-4 to the latest system SearchGPT
our_interpretation: The population is every released transformer LLM as of 2024-07-28, including systems outside OpenAI. The named systems are examples, not an exhaustive list.

The plain reading is that inadequate checking of answers causes recurring arithmetic mistakes, obvious reasoning mistakes, fabrications and occasional false accusations about people throughout that population.
Each listed failure category remains part of the assessment. Evidence of generic hallucinations does not establish the personal-accusation component.
I read 'defame' in its ordinary sense of generating false, reputation-damaging statements about identifiable people. A legal finding of actionable defamation is a separate, stronger requirement.
I read 'leads' as a contributing causal explanation, not a claim that inadequate checking is the sole cause.
The claim concerns systems already released when the post appeared. Later evidence may document those systems or earlier incidents; later model releases cannot settle this historical scope.
The historical scope ends on the post date. No exact starting date is supplied, so the named examples do not impose an artificial lower calendar boundary.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence covering every released transformer LLM in scope establishes recurring failures in the listed categories, including occasional false personal accusations, and controlled interventions or other strong causal evidence show that inadequate answer-checking contributes to those failures. Findings about selected models alone cannot establish the universal claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A well-established counterexample defeats the universal assertion, or controlled evidence disproves the asserted causal contribution for an in-scope model or failure category. Successful answers on a finite test, some ability to correct mistakes, or lack of published failures alone does not establish such a counterexample.

evidence.explanation: The study tested GPT-3, GPT-Neo/J, GPT-2 and a T5-based model and found substantial false-answer rates. This supports recurring factual failures in several families, but does not cover every released model, personal accusations or the asserted cause.

evidence.excerpt: it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors
evidence.explanation: OpenAI acknowledges factual and reasoning failures in GPT-4. The disclosure supports those components for this model, without establishing the universal scope or causal mechanism.

evidence.excerpt: struggle to self-correct their reasoning without external feedback.
evidence.publisher: Huang and colleagues; ICLR 2024, hosted on arXiv
evidence.explanation: Experiments involving GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama-2 support limitations in the tested self-correction methods. They do not establish that absent checking causes every listed failure in every released transformer.

evidence.excerpt: more accurate in verifying the correctness
evidence.locator: Section 5.2, Underlying mechanisms of ProCo success
evidence.explanation: The study reports improved verification and arithmetic reasoning through a structured prompting procedure without external feedback. This qualifies an absolute inability to check answers and is consistent with checking reducing some errors, but does not isolate the cause of all listed failures.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the description of the Boone festival query
evidence.explanation: The report describes SearchGPT presenting box-office closure dates as festival dates in its launch demonstration. This establishes a reported factual error, not repeated failures across all categories or their cause; it is secondary reporting because the primary material was inaccessible through read_page.

evidence.excerpt: accused Walters of embezzling from the SAF.
evidence.explanation: The report reproduces the court's account of ChatGPT generating false embezzlement accusations, while explaining why OpenAI nevertheless won the defamation case. This later ruling is context for the distinction between false personal accusations and actionable defamation, not an in-period outcome or evidence about every model.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Support would require evidence covering every transformer LLM released by July 28, 2024, documenting recurring listed failures and separately checking false personal accusations. Strong causal tests must show that inadequate checking contributes, while controlling for computation, prompt changes and new information. A well-established counterexample or controlled refutation of the claimed causal contribution could contradict the claim.
